text: Zither HarpHello everyone, nice to meet you again.In the previous lesson, we learned how Mark Twain conquered stage fright.Today we'll go deeper into the story by focusing on language.And think about the strategies to deal with such communication barriers.Please get your textbook and worksheet ready.To start with, let's review Mark Twain's first public speech experience,and conclude Mark Twain's state of mind in different stages.30 seconds for you to review yesterday's assignment,and write your answer on the worksheet.Zither HarpAlex, what's your idea?I think Mark Twain's state of mind can be divided into three stages.Before his speech, he was frightened and anxious.In the first five minutes of the speech, he felt agonized.And after these agonizing five minutes, he was confident and relaxed.Well done, could you find us some evidence to support that?Let's start from the first stage, frightened and anxious.In the second paragraph, he says before the lecture,my knees were shaking so that I didn't know whether I could stand up.And he further described stage fright and seasicknessas an awful, horrible disease in the world.Good.Did you notice Mark Twain's description of the auditorium in paragraph 3?Could you read it for us and tell us what it suggests?He says it was dark and lonely behind the scenes in the theater,and I peeked through the little peek holes they have in theater curtainsand looking to the big auditorium.That was dark and empty too.Well, the author describes the auditorium as dark and empty.This is also meant to emphasize the author's fear and anxiety.That's right.The shaking knees, the awful disease, and the dark and empty auditorium.These descriptions all serve to show the author's fear and anxiety.Great.Then, do you still remember what Mark Twain did before his speech to deal with stage fright?He bound himself by a hard and fast contract.Why did Mark Twain sign a hard and fast contract?He bound himself by a contract because he knew that nothing short of compulsion would get him to the theater,which physically prompted him to fulfill his duty.In this case, even if he wanted to give up halfway, he couldn't reject it,for it had become a written duty to be fulfilled.Otherwise, he would suffer great losses.Excellent understanding.Let's focus on the word bound.Bound is the past tense of bind.If you are bound by something such as a rule, an agreement, or a contract,you are forced or required to act in a certain way.We can also say bind somebody to something or somebody be bound by something, usually passive.Please translate the sentence.He was bound by the contract to give a speech in person.What about the second stage?Emily, please.In the second stage, Mark Twain felt agonized because he described the first five minutes as the agonizing five minutes.We can see that from the last paragraph.Agnizing means causing great pain, anxiety, or difficulty.You can say something is agonizing or somebody feels agonized.Then, what did Mark Twain do to survive this painful period?He got a number of friends armed with big clubs, and a special friend to lead the audience into applause to avoid awkward silence on the stage.Why did Mark Twain ask his friends to be armed with big clubs?Because he hoped his friends could pound the clubs they were armed with on the floor.Every time he said anything they possibly guessed, he intended to be funny.Exactly.Be armed with means be equipped with or carry.Mark Twain asked his friend to carry and pound the big clubs when needed.His friends were invited there to help avoid the awkward silence on the stage.What else did he do to fight stage fright?He had the manuscript tucked under a United States flag in front of him.Why did Mark Twain have the manuscript tucked under a United States flag in front of him?Did he turn to the manuscript?Because only in this way could he get at it in case of need, and actually he managed to get started without it.Tuck here means hide or put the edges of the manuscript under a flag, which cannot be noticed by other people, but can be seen by Mark Twain.Please translate the sentence by using the word tuck.After the speech, he had the manuscript tucked under his arm.And you see from the details that although Mark Twain was suffering great pain and anxiety, the condition was still manageable, because he didn't need to refer to the manuscript previously tucked under the flag.So we can also say in this period he felt it is manageable.Who can help with the third stage?Confident and relaxed.JimIn the same sentence, he says, My stage fright left me never to return.Never to return indicates that his confidence outshines his stage fright, which will not return even in the speech later on.The turning point in this stage, I suppose, is the jim he placed in his speech, which touched the audience.And the audience's response to it in turn helped Mark Twain gain confidence and conquer stage fright completely.Why did Mark Twain use the word jim to refer to a moving, pathetic part in the speech?Could you tell us your understanding of the word jim?Literally, jim refers to a precious stone.The contextual meaning of the word jim is a beautiful line or a moving story the speaker plants in the speech to touch the audience.If you describe something or someone as a jim, you mean that they are especially pleasing, good or helpful.So by comparing the moving, pathetic part to a jim, Mark Twain suggests that this moving, pathetic part is the most important part and serves as a touch to the speech.Good job.You just placed a jim in this period of learning.We have covered the efforts Mark Twain took to conquer stage fright in his first public speech.And when it comes to effective communication, don't forget Mark Twain's humor.He employed overstatement to describe the terrible feeling of seasickness, shared some funny experiences, created a contrast between a moving part and a funny coincidence, and so on.Now we can see the clear change of Mark Twain's state of mind and what Mark Twain actually did to make a difference.This time, let's review them in the form of a summary.Please finish activity 2 on your worksheet.Filling the blanks with the appropriate forms of the given words and expressions to complete the passage.Know that there are two options more than you need.One minute for you.Let's check the answers.Mark Twain experienced a stage fright when he worked at The Reporter in San Francisco.He recalled that delivering a speech was so horrible for him at that time that he had to bind himself by a contract.On the day he made a speech, he got to the theater 45 minutes before the hour set for the lecture.He peeked through the holes in the theater curtains.The word peek means take a quick look at something or someone, which serves as another evidence for his anxiety.His knees were shaking while he was to make his bow to the audience.He had got a number of friends armed with big clubs to lead the applause.He had a manuscript hidden under a flag in front of him, where he could get at it in case of need, although he managed to get started without it.Instead of saying had a manuscript tucked under a flag, we also say had a manuscript hidden under a flag.In the middle of the speech, he delivered a moving part, intended to touch the audience, and they did what he had expected.By and by, he stage fright left him, which means eventually he stage fright left him.Fortunately, Mark Twain lived through his first public speaking.By saying lived through his first public speaking, the sentence focuses on the agonizing and unpleasant experience brought by the public speech.Besides Mark Twain, other successful speakers have also shared experiences in making an engaging speech.Let's move on to see what Stephen E.Lucas says to make an engaging speech.Two minutes for you to fill in the blanks in Activity 3.Stephen E.Lucas says that the purpose of public speaking is not to self-promote, but to change someone's assumption, which explains why in his book The Art of Speaking, he doesn't merely talk about the importance of original ideas and a well-organized structure to a successful speech, but also mentioned effective communication skills.They are equally important in making an engaging speech.Delivering a speech is not an entertaining activity, Lucas said.Rather than giving performances, the speaker is expected to convey ideas to the audience.This is why it's important to figure out the types of people in your audience, who may be composed of individuals of different ages, genders, or educational backgrounds.As public speaking covers any occasion, you need to aim your speech at the audience to catch their attention.For instance, if you are asked to speak to a group of young people with learning difficulties, you might need to use simple short sentences.Remember to talk in a natural way, as if you were talking to the youngsters living in your neighborhood.That would help the audience build trust in you.It's also important to involve your audience to make them feel like you are talking to them one-to-one.Speakers do this with gestures, intonations, eye contact, and the like.We are quite familiar with Mark Twain's ways to achieve effective communication in the speech.Now, please use what you have learned in this passage, and finish Lucas' part of this network on this topic.30 seconds for you.Shall we say it together?Lucas not only emphasizes original ideas and well-organized structure, but also attaches importance to figuring out the types of people in the audience, aiming the speech at the audience to catch their attention, speaking with gestures, intonations, and eye contact.I think interaction with the audience is quite important.Through the audience's response, I can make timely adjustments, for example, to help them catch up with what I am talking about, thus making sure that what I want to convey will actually be understood.Thank you for your sharing, and don't forget to write your answer on the worksheet.I bet after this period of learning, you can think of more ways to achieve effective communication in the speech.Today's assignments1.Please think about the communication barriers we discussed in these two lessons, and write two paragraphs according to the following questions.What are the causes of the communication barriers, and what strategies can be used to deal with the barriers?Finish vocabulary focus in a workbook.Now please interact with your teacher and classmates.Suppose you are going to give a public speech on a certain Chinese traditional festival to the elderly in a foreign community.Share the barriers you may encounter, and the strategies for dealing with them.Use some topic-related words learned both in the text and in the exercises.That's all for today.See you next time.Thank you for your sharing.
